The continental AU Data Policy Framework. The passages name Ethiopia only in the African Union's postal address in Addis Ababa; nothing is said of civil registration in Ethiopia.

An education EMIS case study; its only civil registration content is two passing mentions (vital events registration rolled out since 2016, including comprehensive birth registration; student IDs to align with it), with nothing on how or where the record is made and no registration system named.
An essay on algorithmic colonialism; Ethiopia appears only for unmapped gender data and Addis Ababa start-ups, and the one mention of a birth certificate concerns Kenya's biometric ID.

facts.fact: The snapshot, built on a questionnaire the Federal Vital Events Registration Agency completed in December 2018, states that only 100 kebele civil registration offices, all in the Addis Ababa City Administration, use computers to register vital events and issue certificates; it counts 18,617 kebeles, of which 16,883 (about 90 per cent, 92 per cent of them rural) had started civil registration.
facts.system: Computer registration in Addis Ababa kebele civil registration offices

facts.fact: The 100 Addis Ababa kebele offices register vital events and issue certificates on computers at the office; the snapshot describes no national electronic register, and lists a centralised electronic civil registration system as something the World Bank, Gavi and the GFF are supporting to build.
facts.system: Computer registration in Addis Ababa kebele civil registration offices

facts.fact: Outside the 100 Addis Ababa offices registration is on paper: the snapshot says paper-based registration began in most of the country in mid-2016, that the kebele records each event in a bound booklet whose copies go up to the regional office, FVERA and the CSA, and that FVERA names paper-based registration its first challenge.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (FVERA)

facts.fact: The 100 computerised Addis Ababa offices are said to register 'vital events' with no event named; the snapshot gives the events the civil registration system covers as birth, marriage, divorce, death and adoption.
facts.system: Computer registration in Addis Ababa kebele civil registration offices

facts.fact: Civil registration is run by the Federal Vital Events Registration Agency under the Ministry of Peace, with regional vital events registration agencies and a civil status officer in each kebele; the organisational chart is dated 15 December 2018.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (FVERA)

facts.fact: A costed five-year strategic plan for 2014 to 2018 names automation of the civil registration process as a high priority, costed at US$14,074,000 of a US$17,874,000 total (source: FVERA); FVERA had started preparing the 2019-2023 plan.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (FVERA)

facts.fact: FVERA reports a government budget allocation of US$77,000 for 2014 to 2018 against an estimated plan cost of US$18 million, and an expected government allocation of US$1,407,400 towards automation, leaving a gap of US$12,666,600.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (FVERA)

facts.fact: Development partners provided US$2.5 million over 2014 to 2018 (FVERA); the World Bank, Gavi and the Global Financing Facility support building a centralised electronic civil registration system and procuring office equipment, with UNICEF, UNECA, the Netherlands and UNFPA also supporting.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (FVERA)

slug: 2017-01-01 AU - Report on the Status of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics in Africa
note: Continental results of the October 2016 APAI-CRVS monitoring round; Ethiopia appears only in the annex score bands (digitization below 35%, planning, coordination and monitoring below 35%, overall 35-49%). The per-country answers on electronic capture at local offices are not published, and a composite band maps to no aspect value without judgement.

facts.fact: The UNICEF-commissioned evaluation, carried out January to April 2019, reports that computer data entry of registration records was done above the registering office: in Tigray data entry clerks from all sites were converging at the regional headquarters for a mass data verification and entry programme, completed registers went up to federal level for quality assurance (342,363 between July 2017 and June 2018), and the evaluation recommends decentralising computerisation of birth registration data to at least woreda and where possible kebele level.
facts.system: Computer data entry of civil registration records (VERA)

facts.fact: The computer entry the evaluation describes and recommends decentralising is of birth registration data; it names no other event as computerised, and observes that the project design should also have covered death registration.
facts.system: Computer data entry of civil registration records (VERA)

facts.fact: Civil registration is run by the government's Vital Events Registration Agency, renamed the Immigration, Nationality and Vital Events Agency at federal level, with structures and employees at national, regional and woreda levels and the kebele manager acting as civil registrar in over 18,506 urban and rural kebeles legally mandated as registration centres; the evaluation dates this to early 2019.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (VERA / INVEA)

facts.fact: The evaluation reports a National Costed Investment Plan and a national CRVS strategy, and its performance matrix records costed reform plans on CRVS systems as in place at the end of 2018 against none at baseline; it does not say whether the plan covers computerisation.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (VERA / INVEA)

facts.fact: The evaluation finds birth registration included in government plans and budgets, the government having allocated funds to the process, and the Tigray and SNNPR regional offices having put budgetary support for CRVS in their action plans; it gives no amounts and names weak fiscal space as an inhibiting factor.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (VERA / INVEA)

facts.fact: UNICEF's BR4MNCH project, funded by Global Affairs Canada, budgeted US$5,780,970 for Ethiopia over 2014 to 2018 for birth registration, HMIS and their interoperability, with further funds from the Italian Government; 14,796 civil registrars were trained in five regions.
facts.system: Kebele civil registration (VERA / INVEA)

note: Passages file read whole (6,519 lines). The evaluation covers Ethiopia and South Sudan; only what it states of Ethiopia is recorded. It nowhere says an entry is made digitally at the kebele office, so no connected or local fact and no offices fact; it does not use the word paper of Ethiopia's registers, so no paper fact. Whether the Tigray mass data entry is routine or a one-off is not stated; it is recorded as keyed-elsewhere on the document's description of computer data entry as a standing data-quality process. Not facts here: 965,457 children registered over the project, and birth registration in targeted woredas up from 7 to 16 per cent against a 50 per cent target. The South Sudan electronic notification pilot and database belong to SSD. HMIS / DHIS II is a health information system carrying a notification indicator, which no class in the typology describes.
